title: MEND-style gradient factors generate Mirror edit codes
hypothesis: Encoding rank-one edit deltas as compact Mirror coordinates over one shared output basis will preserve edit success, paraphrase generalization, and locality while reducing actual edit-bank bytes versus a MEND-style factor-to-update control.
physical_object: shared 2x2 output basis for edit updates
mirror_coordinate: per-edit polar code (magnitude, angle) decoded to output delta, paired with input key
controls: MEND-style rank-one update factors (input key and output delta)
MEND-style dense update matrix plus key
Mirror polar code plus shared decoder basis

task.edit: key k maps to target y; update is rank-one d k^T / ||k||^2
task.locality: random keys with cosine similarity <0.1 to edited key

development.selection: shared basis is identity; polar code is exact coordinate transform; no tuning

paid_objects: output delta factors or dense updates

success_gate: Every fresh world: Mirror exact-edit success >=99%, paraphrase error <=1.10x MEND, locality drift <=1.10x MEND, and actual N64 payload <=80% MEND factor payload.
failure_gate: Mirror misses quality/locality or N64 bytes fail to improve over rank-one factors; dense matrix comparisons are secondary.
boundaries: Analytic rank-one linear edit screen, not MEND neural-network reproduction.
Key, target delta and decoder state are fully charged.
No factual knowledge or paraphrase-language generalization claim.
